# Delivery plan

[Project](https://github.com/orgs/Pick-Your-AI/projects/6) · [Program](https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-leaderboard/issues/1) · [Structured baseline](../planning/project-backlog.json)

The baseline contains one program, 20 epics and 112 independently reviewable work packages (133 issues), with 474 checklist tasks and 227 native blocked-by relationships. Checklist tasks are not duplicated as issues. A separate issue is appropriate only when a task needs an independent owner or review boundary.

GitHub carries live status, Assignees, native hierarchy and dependencies. The versioned baseline defines deliverables and acceptance. Update the baseline and generated documentation when scope changes, and reconcile its stable IDs with the existing GitHub issues. Do not overwrite live ownership or reset progress from this initial plan.

## Project fields

There are seven single-select fields, including Status. Use built-in Assignees, Labels, Issue type, Parent issue and Sub-issues progress without duplicating ownership. Program and epics use native Feature type; work packages use Task. Labels are selective topical or kind descriptors, never a second status, priority or owner system.

| Field | Options |
| --- | --- |
| Status | Backlog · Ready · In Progress · In Review · Blocked · Done |
| Priority | P0 · P1 · P2 · P3 |
| Readiness | Needs owner · Needs input · Awaiting decision · Ready · Blocked |
| Level | Program · Epic · Work package |
| Phase | Discovery · Foundation · Design and prototype · Public-data alpha · Public beta · Continuous validation · Operations and launch |
| Workstream | Program · 01 Product charter and contribution governance · 02 Repository, delivery Project and engineering foundation · 03 Metric contracts, identity and scope · 04 GitHub App and source capability verification · 05 Reliable live ingestion and event ledger · 06 Historical backfill, reconciliation and coverage · 07 Code, pull request and review recognition · 08 Issue, triage and project stewardship recognition · 09 Research, documentation and quality contributions · 10 Community evidence and editorial recognition · 11 Ranking, filters and fair comparison engine · 12 Read API, snapshots and integration contracts · 13 Information architecture and visual system · 14 Public boards, organization overview and evidence · 15 Contributor portfolios and sharing · 16 Live activity and public display modes · 17 Administration, moderation and contributor controls · 18 Security, privacy and operational safeguards · 19 Verification, accessibility and performance · 20 Hosting, observability and release operations |
| Acceptance Gate | Approved decision · Verified source capability · Automated validation · Evidence review · Accessible user journey · Operational drill · Verified public release |

All initial delivery issues remain Backlog and unassigned. Readiness distinguishes an unresolved decision, a missing prerequisite and a missing accepted owner. Ready requires both accepted ownership and usable inputs. A delivered documentation baseline does not close the package that also requires future implementation.

Views organize the same issue set. Dependency views use genuine prerequisites; source compatibility, related information and optional integrations belong in body links. No artificial dates or iterations are created for a roadmap.
